sections.label: Mutual recognition and limited partnerships
sections.summary: The Bill gives effect to mutual recognition arrangements between BOA and foreign registration authorities, enhances disciplinary proceedings and penalties, and allows limited partnerships to provide architectural services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The proposed changes in the Bill will seek to give effect to arrangements made between BOA and the appropriate foreign registration authority of any country or territory outside Singapore, for the mutual recognition of the qualifications and standards adopted by each of the parties to the arrangement regarding the practice of architecture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It will also enhance disciplinary proceedings and penalties and allow limited partnerships to provide architectural services in Singapore.

sections.label: Disciplinary proceedings and penalties changes
sections.summary: The Bill enhances disciplinary proceedings and penalties by allowing independent investigators, raising maximum penalties, creating a new offence, restricting use of the word architect, and licensing limited partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Next, on Disciplinary Proceedings and Penalties, the proposed changes in this Bill also seek to enhance the disciplinary proceedings and penalties currently provided, which include the following: (a) BOA will be allowed to appoint independent investigators, where necessary, to enable the Board to more effectively deal with disciplinary proceedings; (b) the maximum penalties for certain offences in the Architects Act will be raised to ensure sufficient deterrence; (c) a new offence is created under the new section 12(1A), which makes it an offence for a person to engage the architectural services of another person in relation to any building works unless the other person is authorised under the Act to supply architectural services; and (d) a person will not be allowed to use the word "architect" or any of its derivatives as part of the name of an architectural practice if the person is not authorised under the Act to supply architectural services independently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In view of the fact that the Limited Partnership Act was enacted in 2008 to provide for the establishment and registration of limited partnerships, the Architects Act is now also being updated to allow for the licensing of limited partnerships that provide architectural services in Singapore.

sections.label: Foreign architects working in Singapore
sections.summary: With the amendments, foreign registered architects can work in Singapore, with APEC architects working independently and ASEAN architects collaborating with a licensed Singapore firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the amendments, foreign registered architects will also be able to work in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The APEC Architect Framework allows registered architects in each of the countries to work independently, while ASEAN architects under the ASEAN Framework Agreement have to work in collaboration with a licensed Singapore architectural firm or practice.

sections.label: Recognition of architect qualifications
sections.summary: The amendment allows for recognition of architect qualifications and standards under arrangements between BOA and territories or countries outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Essentially, the amendment to the Bill allows for the recognition of architect qualification and standards with the arrangement between the BOA and those territories or countries outside Singapore.

sections.label: Section 15A and overseas architect standards
sections.summary: Section 15A spells out recognition of registered architects in participating jurisdictions, and questions are raised on qualifications and preserving standards of overseas architects.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 15A, which is a new section that spells out the recognition of registered architects in any participating jurisdiction, is this restricted to foreign architects to obtain any of the qualifications listed in the BOA website?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And importantly, how do we preserve the standards of overseas architects who are practising in Singapore vis-a-vis the Singapore architects?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If there is a tie of votes that she had asked, another round of secret ballot will be carried out.

sections.label: Civil suit to recover money
sections.summary: The person would have to file a civil suit to recover money paid to the unauthorised architect, consistent with recovery processes for other professions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, as she has asked, the person would have to file a civil suit to recover the money paid to the unauthorised architect and this is consistent with the recovery process for other professions as well.

sections.label: Foreign architect registration requirements
sections.summary: A foreign architect must pass the BOA examination on practice laws and pay the prescribed fee before registration under new section 15(2A).

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Following that, the foreign architect will have to pass the examination set by BOA to ensure that he/she has the knowledge of the practice laws, rules and regulations and other conditions of practising in Singapore, and then pay the prescribed fee, before this architect is entitled for registration under the new section 15(2A).

sections.label: BOA investigators and appeals
sections.summary: New section 31(K) lets BOA appoint investigators, such as retired Police Officers, to assist the investigation committee, with appeals to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The new section 31(K) allows BOA to appoint an investigator or more than one investigator to assist the investigation committee, such as assisting to obtain evidences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Such a person may be a retired Police Officer who is familiar with our laws and knows how to conduct proper investigation and search for evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: BOA and the investigation committee will make their own independent decisions and disciplinary decisions after the hearing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But appeals on BOA's decisions can be made to the Minister.
